title: Howard Johnson’s (1925–2022): sold twice, then split · Spectre Brands
description: Howard Johnson’s had 1,040 restaurants in 1979. Two sales in six years and a 1985 split left it to franchisees. The last restaurant closed in 2022.

card.blurb: Once the largest restaurant chain in America, with 28 flavors and an orange roof on every highway. It was sold twice in six years, split in two, and left to its franchisees.

hero.dates: Soda fountain bought in 1925. Last restaurant closed in 2022.
hero.standfirst: The roof was orange so that drivers could see it from a distance. By the end there was one left to see.
hero.deck: Howard Johnson’s was the orange-roofed highway chain that taught America to eat the same meal in every state, and its last restaurant closed in Lake George, New York, in 2022. It had 1,040 restaurants when a British tobacco group paid $630 million for it, announced in 1979. Six years later it was sold again for half that and cut in two: the restaurants one way, the name and the hotels another. Most of this story predates electronic filings, so it rests on contemporary press, a reference history and later reporting, and it says where they disagree.

findings.title: It stopped building in 1974 and never restarted.
findings.text: Howard B. Johnson froze expansion after the oil embargo and later told Forbes he had overreacted. The company sat on $90M of cash and securities while fast-food and lodging rivals built.[^1]

findings.title: The restaurants were the weak half.
findings.text: Howard Johnson’s restaurants produced 78% of the restaurant group’s sales in 1977 but 57% of its pretax profit. The motels produced 16% of company sales in 1978 and more than 43% of earnings.[^1]

findings.title: Two sales in six years halved the price.
findings.text: Imperial paid $630M and sold for $314M. Pretax earnings fell from $34M in 1979 to $14.7M in 1980 and did not fully recover.[^1][^2]

findings.title: The 1985 deal separated the name from the kitchens.
findings.text: Marriott kept 418 company restaurants to convert to other brands. Prime Motor Inns took the trademark, the hotels and 199 franchised restaurants it did not want.[^2][^4]

findings.title: The franchisees kept it alive for 37 more years.
findings.text: Their company, Franchise Associates, held a perpetual license from 1986. There were about 110 franchised restaurants in 1991, eight in 2005, three in 2007 and one from 2016 to 2022.[^1][^6][^7][^11]
